Eating across more colors each week made hitting 30 plants feel like collecting, not a chore.
Going back to basics for a couple of weeks and then adding foods back one at a time finally helped me see which ones actually bothered me.
I never knew how few different plants I was eating until the weekly count showed me. Now I hit thirty most weeks.
Tracking the smell of my gas felt silly at first, but it turned out to be the clue that helped me spot my pattern.
The garden blooming when I kept feeding the same crews made the science click in a way a chart never did.
Reintroducing onion and garlic slowly, instead of cutting them forever, took the fear out of eating again.
